# HoneyChain Intelligence Layer (Phase 7)

## What the model is and is not

* `IsolationForest` over `temperature, humidity, weight, audio_frequency`: a **telemetry
  anomaly detector**. It is **not** a disease diagnosis and **not** a honey-quality test
  (honey quality comes from laboratory results).
* Trained **only on synthetic data** (`data/synthetic_hive_telemetry.csv`, generated by
  `train_model.py` with a fixed seed). `real_world_evaluation` is `null`, because no labelled
  real-world hive data exists (see `data/DATASETS.json`; no dataset has ground-truth health
  labels). All figures under `synthetic_evaluation` were measured on data from the same
  generator and **are not real-world accuracy**. Tests fail if a metric appears anywhere else.

## Decision policy (rules first)

| Layer | Role |
|---|---|
| Deterministic rules (`rules.py`) | Authoritative. Hard biological limits; only they (and the swarm rate detector) raise CRITICAL by default. |
| ML band `NORMAL` / `WATCH` / `ANOMALOUS` | Complementary risk signal with its score and model version. `ANOMALOUS` raises the status to at most `HONEYCHAIN_ML_MAX_ESCALATION` (default `WARNING`). `WATCH` never changes status. |
| Suppression | ML is **not applied** to the verdict when any feature was imputed or the reading has sensor data-quality flags; an odd score then more likely reflects the sensor than the colony. |

Bands come from the model metadata: `ANOMALOUS` means `decision_function < 0` (the model's
contamination boundary); `WATCH` means below the 5% quantile of scores on normal training
readings. They are derived from the data rather than chosen by hand. They are **not
calibrated probabilities**, and no confidence percentage is produced.

## Data-quality flags (not health conclusions)

Device readings carry `sensor_flags`: `MISSING_*`, `IMPLAUSIBLE_JUMP_*`, `FLATLINE_*`
(Phase 4) and `STAT_OUTLIER_*`. The last is a robust modified z-score (median/MAD,
|z| > 3.5, Iglewicz & Hoaglin) against the hive's own last 20+ readings. An outlier may be
a failing sensor **or** a real colony event, so flags never change the rule verdict. They
only stop the ML layer from turning the reading into a health conclusion.

## Model compatibility and integrity

* A scikit-learn pickle is only valid for the version that wrote it. `requirements.txt`
  pins `scikit-learn==<exact version>`, and the metadata records the training environment.
* `honeychain.ml` checks, **before unpickling** (unpickling executes code):
  metadata `schema_version >= 2` with a declared `data_source`; runtime scikit-learn equal
  to the training version; SHA-256 of both artefacts equal to the recorded hashes. It then
  unpickles with `InconsistentVersionWarning` escalated to an error. Any failure leaves the
  model unavailable with a specific reason, and the rules run alone.
* Training is deterministic (`random_state=42`, `n_jobs=1`, fixed synthetic epoch
  `2000-01-01`). Retraining in a clean interpreter reproduces the model and dataset
  **byte for byte**, and a test enforces this.

**Upgrading scikit-learn:** bump the pin, run `python train_model.py`, and commit the new
`models/*` together with `model_metadata.json` and the updated `data/DATASETS.json` hash.

## Configuration

`HONEYCHAIN_RULE_*` (threshold overrides; invalid values stop startup),
`HONEYCHAIN_ML_MAX_ESCALATION` (`WARNING`|`CRITICAL`), `HONEYCHAIN_SENSOR_ROBUST_Z`,
`HONEYCHAIN_SENSOR_ROBUST_MIN_HISTORY`. `GET /api/ml/status` reports the model version,
data source, compatibility, bands, fusion policy, and every active threshold with its
source (`default` or `env override`).

## Known limitations

* No real-world validation: detection quality on real hives is **unknown**.
* Point-in-time features only (no temporal model); temporal signals come from the
  deterministic swarm, jump, flatline and robust-outlier detectors.
* Devices without an audio channel (like the prototype captured in `data/raw_data.txt`)
  have `audio_frequency` imputed, so ML is suppressed for their readings and the reason
  says so. On such deployments the intelligence layer is effectively rules + statistics.
